page.name: Marketplaces & platforms
page.metaDescription: Buyer and seller notifications, order and dispute updates over the provider accounts your platform already holds.
page.lede: A marketplace messages two audiences about the same event for opposite reasons: the buyer wants it to arrive, the seller wants proof that it did. That makes the receipt the part worth getting right.

bullets: Order placed, confirmed and shipped — to both sides
Dispute, refund and chargeback status changes
Payout and settlement notices to sellers
Review and rating prompts after completion

sections.h: The receipt is the audit trail
p: When a seller disputes whether they were told something, the answer has to be a record rather than a recollection. The platform logs each send, normalizes provider delivery receipts into one status and can push those events to your own endpoint — so the record lives in your system too.

sections.h: Where your platform ends and ours starts
p: Your platform decides who is notified and what the notification says. On the SMS channel the messaging layer decides how it leaves the building — which connected account carries it, at what pace, and what receipt comes back.

faq.q: Can we tell whether a specific seller was notified?
faq.a: Sends and their statuses are logged, and receipts can be pushed to an endpoint you control. Note that a receipt means the destination network accepted the message, not that it was read.

faq.q: Is there a callback retry policy?
faq.a: Callback delivery is deliberately not treated as fire-and-forget; the reliability model and its limits are set out in the callback guide.

faq.q: Can different sellers use their own provider accounts?
faq.a: Connections are held per tenant. Whether each seller is a separate tenant, and therefore has their own connections and API keys, is a design decision on your side.
